title: Key a pulley onto a shaft and lock it with its set screw
instruction: Fit the pulley to the shaft and lock it with its set screw.
context: Keying a pulley, gear or coupling hub to a shaft and locking it with its set screw is how belt and chain drives are put back together after a repair, often at the bench before the motor or gearbox goes back in place. It is core work for industrial machinery mechanics (SOC 49-9041, 412,650 US jobs), machinery maintenance workers (49-9043, 58,040) and millwrights (49-9044, 37,930): 508,620 together (BLS OEWS May 2023), whose O*NET tasks include "Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs" and "Replace defective parts of machine". The instruction leaves the procedure out. The key goes into its closed keyseat first and is pressed fully home; the pulley is turned until its keyway, inside the bore, lines up with the key and is pushed over it to the shoulder (forced over a key that is not home, it cocks the key); the set screw over the key is turned in, regripping the driver between wrist strokes, until the driver's preset clutch slips.
setup: Positions in cm in the task frame (x forward from the midpoint between the arm bases, y left, heights above the bench top). Shaft: steel, 2.0 cm diameter (h7), axis along x at y 0, 4.5 cm up, from x 20.0 (free end) to its far end, clamped in a blue shaft support block (3 x 6 x 6.5 cm, at x 37.5-40.5, on a 7 x 10 x 0.8 cm foot; the shaft can't turn or slide); a 3.0 cm shoulder collar 0.8 cm long at x 31.5. Keyseat: 0.6 cm wide (N9), 0.35 cm deep, 2.55 cm long on top of the shaft, from x 28.85 to 31.40, closed at both ends (end-milled), so the key can only go in from above. Key: steel parallel key 0.6 x 0.6 x 2.5 cm (ISO/R 773 form B), lying flat on a green 8 x 8 x 0.2 cm mat at x 25.5, y -15, its long side along x. Pulley: a stock aluminium pulley, a 6.0 cm rim 1.2 cm wide in front of a 3.6 cm boss 1.6 cm long (2.8 cm overall), bore 2.0 cm (H7) with a 0.6 cm keyway (JS9) 0.28 cm deep; on the shaft with its rear face at x 26.2 (2.65 cm short of the keyseat), turned 65 deg about the shaft so its keyway and set screw point up and to the left (+y). Set screw: M5 x 0.8 hexagon socket cup point (ISO 4029), 2.5 mm socket, in the boss over the keyway, 0.8 cm in front of the rear face, backed out until its tip is 0.3 mm above the keyway's roof. Driver: a stock T-handle preset-torque driver set to 2.0 N m (its clutch slips past that), a red handle 8 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm and a 2.5 mm hex bit 6 cm below it, standing in a grey cup (2.0 x 2.0 x 6.5 cm outside, 0.3 cm walls) at x 23.5, y 15, its handle resting across the cup's rim along x.
scoring: Judged at the end with calipers, a 0.5 mm feeler gauge and the 2.0 N m driver. 0 if at any point the key was cocked (the pulley forced over a key standing proud of its seat), or the key or the driver fell off the bench. Otherwise: key home: in the keyseat, square to it (within 3 deg), its top no more than 2.8 mm above the shaft's top (2.5 mm when fully home; a pulley that has passed over the key shows it home). Keyed and seated: the pulley's keyway over the key, and the feeler gauge doesn't enter between its rear face and the shoulder. Tight: the set screw turned in until the driver's clutch slipped with the pulley keyed and seated, and not backed off since (checked afterwards: the same driver slips before the screw turns); in the simulation, 30 deg past the screw's tip touching the key. 1.0: key home, keyed and seated, tight, the driver's bit out of the screw (at least 2 cm from its socket) and the driver on the bench, every gripper point at least 2 cm from the pulley, key and driver, and nothing moved more than 5 mm over the last second; held 1 s. 0.75: key home, keyed, seated and tight, short of the rest. 0.5: key home, keyed and seated, screw not tight. 0.25: key home only. 0: anything else, including a pulley seated with no key.
reset_notes: Back the set screw out 300 deg from tight (its tip then 0.3 mm above the keyway's roof), slide the pulley back until its rear face is at the start mark (x 26.2) with its keyway turned 65 deg toward +y, lift the key out and lay it on the mat, and stand the driver in its cup.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. PhysX can't model a 6 N9 interference fit, a thread or a clutch, so task code does (stated in pulley_logic.py): the simulated keyseat is 6.4 mm wide for a 6.0 mm key, 1.5 mm longer at its free end than drawn and its top edges broken 0.6 mm (the arm places a key to about a millimetre; a key caught on a square lip sits perched), and a hidden pad in it holds a key 1.5 mm proud until it is pressed down with 10 N, then lets it reach the floor, where a key that is home is fixed in place. The pulley rides two joints on the shaft (slide and turn, lightly damped, no bore contact); its keyway can pass the key's end only with the keyway within 4 deg of the key, the key home and the screw clear of the keyway (else the pulley stops at the key; pushed on with about 20 N while lined up over a proud key, the key cocks). The set screw advances 0.8 mm a turn while the driver's bit is in its socket (the bit is held on the screw's axis once it drops in within 2 mm and 10 deg (a bit pushed onto the screw's face off the socket rests there until it lines up), and comes out when the hand holding the handle lifts it 5 mm); the clutch slips 30 deg past the screw touching the key (estimated angle to 2.0 N m), and a tight screw fixes the pulley where it is. Masses: key 20 g (a real one is 7 g), pulley 150 g, driver 60 g. The free end has a stop (a real pulley could slide off).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms moved toward the middle of the bench and down, but never touched the key, the pulley or the driver); demo: 1.0
